name: PINK OYSTER

plan.note: share of the old 100-bag split. The 130-bag plan (Joseph, 5 Nov 2026) is 52 blue, 46 lion's mane, 16 comb tooth, plus a 16-bag slot whose species you pick (PRODUCTION SEQUENCE)

blurb: FASTEST IN CATAWBA'S DATA. MADE FOR HEAT.

overview.v: Little detailed data exists. Treated like other oysters. Pleurotus biology.
In 1963 Bano and Srivastava grew P. flabellatus (a pink oyster now placed in P. djamor) on paddy straw in India.
Cap n Stem's advice to growers in hot places: "grow some pinks." A Memphis grower cranked out oysters in a greenhouse he could not hold below 27-32 °C.
w: Bluff City Fungi podcast with Cap n Stem

overview.v: Catawba's review recommended adding pink oyster. It is not in the core 130-bag plan; it can run in the 16-bag slot any week you choose.

cultivation.v: Does not survive cryo. Keep agar plugs in sterile water.

cultivation.n: Textbook says treat like other oysters (F18-0159). That is not a measured figure.

timeline.v: 18 days (15-21), the fastest of all their species.

climate.v: Same as the other oysters: about 19 °C (66 °F) for blocks, about 18 °C (65 °F) for grain. Catawba incubates every species at about 18 °C (65 °F).
climate.n: Joseph, 9 Nov 2026: use the same figures as the other oysters unless Catawba has data.

climate.v: Same as the other oysters: 13-18 °C (55-65 °F). Catawba fruits it in rooms at 14-17 °C (58-62 °F).
climate.n: Joseph, 9 Nov 2026: use the same figures as the other oysters unless Catawba has data.

climate.v: Same as the other oysters: keep low. High CO2 gives long stems with no caps.
climate.n: Joseph, 9 Nov 2026: use the same figures as the other oysters unless Catawba has data.

climate.v: Same as the other oysters: none needed in incubation.
climate.n: Joseph, 9 Nov 2026: use the same figures as the other oysters unless Catawba has data.

yield_.n: Cap n Stem gives no figure.

yield_.v: Knocked only Apr-Sep; none in winter. About 50 blocks a week in summer 2026.

hazards.v: "Look pretty, but don't hold up in the pan." Old pinks smell bad in the bin.

hazards.n: No species-specific problems recorded. General oyster hazards are in the BLUE OYSTER file.

notes.v: Highest $ per block per 30 shelf days in Catawba's ranking at their prices, because it turns so fast. At Joseph's flat oyster price it ranks third, behind blue and lion's mane.
